candidates.name: Cervical dystonia
support_spans: bouts of an extremely stiff, nonpainful neck that tilted her head involuntarily leftwards, upwards, and backwards in hyperextension
Involuntary posturing with head, neck, and spine arched backward
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms of a stiff, nonpainful neck and involuntary posturing are characteristic of cervical dystonia.

candidates.name: Ocular torticollis
support_spans: Conjugate deviation of the eyes upward or laterally
candidates.why: The patient's eye deviation is a common feature of ocular torticollis.

candidates.name: Tardive dystonia
support_spans: After starting a new medication at low dose (25 mg per day divided into two doses) for two days, the dose was increased to 25 mg twice daily on the third day
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms of dystonic posturing appeared after starting a new medication, which could be related to tardive dystonia.

candidates.name: Acute dystonic reaction
support_spans: She was readmitted the same evening
candidates.why: The patient's sudden onset of dystonic symptoms could be indicative of an acute dystonic reaction.

candidates.name: Sandifer syndrome
support_spans: Involuntary posturing with head, neck, and spine arched backward
Difficulty in opening or closing the mouth
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms of involuntary posturing and difficulty with mouth movement could be indicative of Sandifer syndrome, which can be diagnosed with imaging studies.

candidates.name: Subacute sclerosing panencephalitis
support_spans: Conjugate deviation of the eyes upward or laterally
Involuntary posturing with head, neck, and spine arched backward
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms of eye deviation and involuntary posturing could be indicative of subacute sclerosing panencephalitis, which can be diagnosed with imaging and laboratory studies.
